- [Why controllers use decorators](md/decisions/why-decorators.md): Decorators for implementation metadata, with a compiled orchestrator.
- [Why discovery does not execute application code](md/decisions/why-no-code-execution-in-discovery.md): Static analysis keeps tooling safe, fast and deterministic.
- [Why authentication is deny-by-default](md/decisions/why-deny-by-default.md): Safe defaults instead of safe habits.
- [Why dispatch is optional](md/decisions/why-dispatch-optional.md): Simple systems should not need a message broker.
- [Why Spring Boot remains independent](md/decisions/why-spring-independent.md): Services are ordinary Spring Boot applications.
- [Why the bootstrap is minimal](md/decisions/why-minimal-bootstrap.md): main.ts is one call; the framework does the rest.
- [Why the CLI manages project infrastructure](md/decisions/why-cli-manages-infrastructure.md): One tool creates, validates, runs, secures and packages.
- [Why there is no TypeScript transactional outbox](md/decisions/why-no-typescript-outbox.md): The outbox lives where the business data lives (Spring services with a database); the TypeScript orchestrator is stateless by design.
- [Controller or service?](md/decisions/controller-or-service.md): What belongs in a controller and what in a service or provider, in the orchestrator and in Spring - with a rule of thumb, a worked example and the consequences of getting it wrong.
- [Validate in the gateway or in the service?](md/decisions/gateway-or-service-validation.md): Where input validation should live when a request crosses the orchestrator and a Spring service - what each layer is responsible for, what it costs to duplicate, and a decision flow.
- [HTTP call or Dispatch event?](md/decisions/http-or-dispatch.md): When one service should call another and wait, and when it should publish an event and move on - the consequences for coupling, failure, consistency and testing.
- [Redis Streams, RabbitMQ or Kafka?](md/decisions/redis-rabbitmq-or-kafka.md): How to choose a Dispatch provider - ordering, retention, operations, throughput, replay and what each adapter in PSO actually guarantees - and how to migrate if you chose wrong.
- [Transactional outbox or direct publish?](md/decisions/outbox-or-direct-publish.md): When publishing straight to the broker is enough and when the event must be stored in the same database transaction - the failure it prevents, what it costs, and why the Node orchestrator has no outbox.
- [Spring Data JPA or JDBC?](md/decisions/jpa-or-jdbc.md): Choosing between an ORM and plain SQL in a PSO Spring service - what each costs, where each fits, and how to use both in the same service.
- [Synchronous or asynchronous operations?](md/decisions/sync-or-async.md): Whether an operation should finish before the response is sent, and how to model the work that cannot - without pretending that PSO has a job queue it does not have.
- [Local or distributed rate limiting?](md/decisions/local-or-distributed-rate-limit.md): When per-instance token buckets are enough and when several instances must share one budget through Redis - including failure policy and client identity behind proxies.
- [Pretty logs or structured JSON?](md/decisions/pretty-or-json-logs.md): Which log format to use where - a person reading a terminal, a machine reading a stream, or both - and the rules PSO applies by default.
- [Development or production configuration?](md/decisions/dev-or-production-config.md): What changes between a developer's machine and production in PSO - profiles, layers, secrets, security requirements, logging and limits - and how to make the difference explicit instead of accidental.

## AI Context

- [PSO AI Context](md/ai-context/overview.md): Give coding assistants accurate, version-matched knowledge of PSO instead of letting them guess.
- [Context builder](md/ai-context/builder.md): Choose and combine contexts, see the size, copy or download in the format your assistant reads.
- [Assistant files and the CLI](md/ai-context/assistant-files.md): pso ai:context and pso ai:init: generate AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Copilot instructions or generic Markdown.
- [llms.txt and machine-readable files](md/ai-context/llms-files.md): The LLM-friendly artifacts generated with this portal, and how they are produced.
- [Accuracy and security of AI context](md/ai-context/accuracy-and-security.md): What the context guarantees, what it refuses to say, and how repository content is kept from steering the assistant.

## Reference

- [Choose an integration approach](md/reference/choosing-an-approach.md): Decide where code belongs and when to use HTTP, Dispatch, an outbox or a broker provider.
- [Troubleshooting by symptom](md/reference/troubleshooting.md): Diagnose routing, modules, DTO validation, JWT, connectivity, databases, migrations, brokers, telemetry, installation and updates - each with symptoms, causes, diagnostic commands, log lines, the fix, how to verify and how to prevent it.
- [Validation errors, one by one](md/reference/diagnostics-catalog.md): Eleven real mistakes in modules, routes, services and security, the exact message `pso validate` prints for each, why it happens, how to fix it and how to prevent it.
- [Environment variables and naming rules](md/reference/environment-variables.md): Every environment variable PSO reads, the canonical configuration key behind it, and the naming rules that keep configuration consistent.
- [Why the orchestrator refuses to start](md/reference/startup-failures.md): Eight start-up failures of the orchestrator - TLS, JWT algorithm, key file, JWKS URL, rate limit, log level, port and a misspelled setting - each reproduced, with the exact log line, cause, fix and prevention.
- [Documentation components](md/reference/documentation-components.md): The one component for each kind of representation in this documentation (file tree, architecture, flow, terminal command, output, source, callout, table), its canonical syntax, and the rules that keep hand-drawn diagrams out.
- [Decorators and API reference](md/reference/decorators.md): The decorators and functions of @pso/http and @pso/core with exact semantics.
- [Error standard (RFC 9457)](md/reference/error-standard.md): One error format for the TypeScript orchestrator and every Spring service: Problem Details with stable PSO codes.
- [TypeScript and Java conformance](md/reference/conformance.md): Which behaviors are proven identical in the Node orchestrator and the Spring starters by shared fixtures, and which are not.
- [Configuration reference](md/reference/config.md): Typed configuration keys, defaults and constraints.
- [Diagnostics reference](md/reference/diagnostics.md): Stable diagnostic codes raised by PSO, extracted from the compiled sources.
- [Extending PSO](md/reference/extending.md): Where to add resource kinds, commands, guards, checks and documentation pages - with a worked example of a new command and the tests that will tell you what you forgot.
- [Version migration](md/reference/migration.md): How schema versions are handled when upgrading, a procedure for upgrading a workspace safely, and a checklist of behavior that changed in recent framework work that generated projects may need to adopt.
